fix_note: 'Listen again' re-fetched the feed with no trace the click did anything — the same dispatches came back and nothing on screen changed. Previously a pick only scrolled to and ringed a stats card for four seconds — and on an instance with no recorded interactions there was no card at all, so the pick landed silently on the empty state.

(or 'at its lowest').

The player-mail gift and COD amount fields coerced every keystroke (a typed -1 became 01, letters became 0, and 999999999 sailed through to a server refusal). Both fields now hold the typed text and parse only at Send: a non-number, a negative, or an amount over the server's governing 1,000,000 CC bound (badNumericField, server/domains/mail.js) is refused by name under the fields — 'Gift amount must be a number from 0 to 1,000,000 CC.' — with the form kept open and the typed text untouched; a hint states the range up front. Same typed-string shape as the housing place inputs.

The composer now fetches the signed-in id on mount and explains at the recipient field the moment the picked recipient is yourself — 'That's you — player mail can't be sent to yourself, so Send stays off until you pick someone else.' — with Send disabled until the recipient changes (the ticket's explain-before-Send leg; the server refusal stays as backstop and no money/escrow semantics changed).

A blank partner is refused in the open with what to do; the empty state now points at the form.

Partners rendered as raw ids ('player:<uuid>', 'npc:<id>'), and a past marriage showed a bare 'player:' because the server presenters strip the other player's raw account id without putting a name in its place. Rows now carry partner_name/partner_handle resolved the way mail names correspondents: players through the users table (display name, else @handle), an NPC's id is its world-visible name, an unresolvable player carries nulls and the UI falls back to 'A Concord member' — never the raw id. All four panels (courtships, marriages, past marriages, pregnancies) plus the dissolve and heart-event modals render the shared partnerLabel. The privacy strip itself stands. Two shipped suites' raw-form expectations were updated to the name form, disclosed here. NAMED, NOT FIXED (desk's call): the same strip removes the partner id from the owner's OWN marriage rows, which the conceive/dissolve actions post back — a privacy-posture question beyond this display ticket.

The lattice Overview showed platform-wide consent corpus counts (Total rows 562,259, consented 2,868, per-table totals) with no scope label, so a regular user could read them as their own corpus. The endpoint is deliberately a public anonymized aggregate, so the surface now takes the ticket's labelling leg: a scope line under the heading states these are platform-wide totals across every creator on this instance — not just your DTUs — and points to the Consent tab for the viewer's own state; the stat cards and the per-table heading carry the platform-wide label too. The invariant Overview's Monitors-active badge showed '70%' with 0/0 monitors: the badge carried the global lock-70 CSS class, whose ::after paints a hardcoded '70%' regardless of data. The badge no longer uses that class; it renders the real active percentage as a chip (same styling) computed from the monitor summary, and only when monitors exist — with none, the badge shows 0/0 and no percentage at all. The lock-70 class itself stays for the Home locked cards, a different surface outside this ticket.

The social Inbox badge read 25 against 75 unread in the panel: the badge (the social page's Inbox tab) read only the social-store count, while the panel counts both stores (social + the platform queue). Three legs now measure the same set: the page badge adds the platform queue's unread, mirroring NotificationBell; the panel fetches both routes' full 200 window instead of 50, so its header chip no longer undercounts past a page; and the server's getUnreadCount applies the same notification-type preference filter as getNotifications (muted types no longer inflate the badge against the list).

The goddess dispatch feed was stale and uniform — every dispatch 'I observe: the cycle continues.', ecosystem 0.00 — because composeAndRecord read the ecosystem score from STATE.worlds, which in the real server is the sub-worlds store keyed by userId (values are arrays of a user's worlds), so the worldId lookup never hit and the score was always 0. The broadcaster now reads the world's real ecosystem mean from player_world_metrics via score-engine's worldEcosystemPercent (the sanctioned reader; an empty sample is not a score) and maps it onto the tone scale, so dispatches carry the world's actual tone and score. With no metrics sample it falls back to an in-memory world object that genuinely carries a numeric score, else the previous neutral 0. Matches how viability-cycle and analytics already read the same table.

Commune replies were identical canned text for every commune type: the intent never reached the reply, so greet/petition/offering/question all returned the reception (usually greet) template. The commune action now answers the intent — an author-written dialogue template whose trigger is the intent speaks for that intent when present; otherwise a deterministic intent line derived from intent + reception + the deity's tone axes is added (a petition heard or unheard, a question answered plainly, veiled, or not at all, an empty-handed offering noted). An offering is now acknowledged whenever the deity does not refuse it, not only in the received band. All four intents produce distinct utterances, pinned by test.

The Map view showed no points for an imported timeline: timeline-from-wikipedia asked Wikipedia only for the article extract and stamped every imported event lat/lng null, so Map view was empty for every import, even for a place. The import now also requests the article's coordinates in the same query; when the article is geotagged, its events are stamped with those coordinates, named by the article title, so map-points returns them and they plot in the Map view (any event can still be moved or cleared there). Articles without coordinates import exactly as before — no location is ever invented. The import panel's success line says the events are plotted when they are. Pins cover a geotagged article plotting and a coordinate-less article staying point-free.

The Listings tab now renders the canonical store's rows too, in a 'From Search' group honouring the tab's search text (address, city, price, beds/baths/sqft, status), and the empty state shows only when both stores are empty. A Search listing can be removed from the store from the Desk with a two-step confirm; editing stays in Search, where the listing was created, and the group says so. Pins cover the tab rendering a Search-only listing and the confirmed removal.

The post card's heart button only opened the emoji picker, so clicking it twice opened and closed the picker — no count, no removal — and a failed react was swallowed silently. The heart now toggles the heart reaction itself (the social react macro toggles the same kind off and switches from any other kind, matching X/Twitter's heart), the picker lives on its own chevron button with the current kind titled 'click again to remove', and a failed react now shows the worded notice instead of looking like a dead toggle. Server toggle verified working at audit-time main and branch head by harness before the fix; the defect was the button's wiring.

Another user's profile page showed no Follow/Message buttons — only 'Copy ID' in the menu. Root cause: the ['auth-me'] react-query key is shared, and the shell (Topbar/RailAccount) caches the full { ok, user } envelope under it while the social profile page cached only res.data.user. With the app's 60s staleTime, in-app navigation served the shell's envelope to the page with no refetch; the page read viewer id off the envelope, got undefined, passed currentUserId=undefined to UserProfile, and the profile hid its entire Follow/Message/Mute/Block/Report row. The page now caches the envelope like every other consumer of the key and resolves the viewer from either cached shape, so Follow + Message render for a signed-in viewer on someone else's profile (and stay hidden on your own). Related sighting, not fixed here: app/messages/page.tsx reads userData?.id off the same envelope cache (its currentUserId resolves empty the same way) — same genus, different surface, for the desk to route.

World Creator had no Save-as-DTU for the world being authored — the only SaveAsDtuButton in the lens saved Reddit inspiration posts, and the world-creator domain carries no DTU path for a draft. The DraftEditor header now has Save as DTU: it saves the draft itself through the standing dtu.create path as a PRIVATE DTU — the author's own work, so own-work provenance (source world-creator:draft, no public-data framing) — with the full draft (scene, rules, terrain, factions) in the machine payload (kind world_creator_draft) and a plain-language summary; the save is verified by read-back before it is claimed, a refused save lands in the editor's alert, and the success note names the DTU id and says the draft itself is unchanged (each save is a new snapshot), matching the SRS deck publish pattern.

Per-crisis Incident reports list no longer silently drops reports filed without a crisis (filed from the all-reports view, or before a crisis was selected): the triage board always listed them, the per-crisis list filtered strictly on data.crisisId and read 'No incident reports filed for this crisis yet.' Now this crisis's reports list first (ids compared as strings, the server's own convention), unscoped reports appear in a labelled 'Filed without a crisis' group with an 'Attach to this crisis' action that re-sends the full record with the crisisId and crisis tag added, other crises' reports never render, and the empty state says when unscoped reports are listed below instead of claiming none exist. Matches the unlinked-incident handling in PagerDuty/Jira: unlinked reports stay visible and linkable, never merged silently. Pins 4/4 new, pristine control 3 fail / 1 pass (the pass is the preserved all-reports behaviour); CrisisOpsRoster's 2 failures at head are pre-existing (identical on the pristine panel).

A COD / attachment mail now has two answers, not one: beside Claim the recipient gets a two-step Decline. Declining returns the whole escrow in one transaction — the gift CC is credited back to the sender and the DTU escrow stamps clear (the DTUs never left the sender), the recipient is charged nothing and the COD is never collected — and the mail lands in a new terminal 'declined' state (migration 502 widens the status CHECK and stamps declined_at), which claim then refuses by name. Same return-to-sender shape as Gmail's and Outlook's refusal of a COD/parcel delivery: the package and its postage go back, the recipient pays nothing. Pins: server decline suite 5/5 against a real migrated DB (escrow refunded in full, recipient balance untouched, CC conserved, claim-after-decline refused, second decline idempotent, sender cannot decline, claimed mail cannot be declined), full-build 7/7 + realdb 12/12 + macros/stub green; FE decline pin 1/1, coverage 6/6. Disclosed shipped-pin updates: both mail catalog pins now list the true 10-verb surface — mail-full-build's pin was already stale at head (it omitted the draft verbs from FIX-mail-002; it fails identically on the pristine tree). Pristine controls fail: server decline suite entire, FE decline pin.

Player mail now threads. A reply carries the mail it answers (new parent_id column, migration 503) and the folder list nests each reply directly under its original with a thread marker, however new the reply is; the opened mail shows its thread — 'In reply to' for a reply, and the replies under an original, assembled across both folders. Reply and Forward now exist in the detail pane: Reply seeds the composer with the other party, a Re: subject and the quoted original, and the send stores the parent — the server validates it (the parent must exist and the sender must be a party to it, else the send is refused as parent_not_found: threading cannot be forged into a stranger's conversation); Forward quotes the original with no recipient and no thread link, and never carries attachments (escrowed DTUs/CC cannot honestly move that way). The thread link survives the autosaved draft round-trip, and a seeded reply says so in the open ('This is a reply — it will thread under the original mail'). Same conversation shape as Gmail threading. Pins: server threading suite 3/3 on a real migrated DB (parent stored and carried by list/sent/get, dangling + forged parents refused with no row written, draft round-trip), full mail set green (full-build 7/7, realdb 12/12, macros, decline 5/5, stub), FE threading 2/2 + composer seed 1/1 + coverage/decline/017/010 suites; pristine controls fail entire (server 0/3, FE 0/3). Sync note: the landing cherry-pick merged with FIX-mail-007's composer change (draft restore fills only empty fields) — both behaviours preserved and re-verified on the merged tree.

An unconnected Gmail no longer costs a storm of failing calls. Two layers, matching how the platform already treats missing_api_key: (1) the /api/lens/run status mapper (server/lib/lens-run-http.js) now answers the connector not-linked family — no_token, connector_not_configured, gmail_disabled, no_user, on the error or reason channel — as HTTP 200 with the { ok:false, reason } body instead of 400, so the browser logs no resource error for a state the client renders as its connect wall (Slack's no_token gets the same quiet treatment); (2) the mail client stops firing behind the wall — once a not-connected answer lands, the load effects (list, profile, labels) check a ref mirror of that fact and fire nothing more, where a page load previously cost five failing requests (list + profile + labels, then profile + labels again when the connected flag flipped) and every folder click added another. A successful list load clears the mirror, so Retry after connecting elsewhere still recovers. Note on the ticket's toast half: at branch state the NOT_CONNECTED codes are already consumed into the connect wall by handleFail and no toast fires on this path — that half does not reproduce; the failing-call half is the live defect and is what is fixed here. Pins: new server unit suite 3/3 (family on both channels + neighbours unchanged: validation 422, balance 409, not_found 404, unmapped refusal still 400, near-miss token no_token_budget still 400) with the shipped failure-status suite green beside it; FE quiet-load pin 1/1 (exactly one probe round: threads/profile/labels once each, wall shown, a folder click fires nothing) + mail-client/full-build/compose-not-connected/MailPage suites green (26/26); pristine controls fail (server family tests, FE quiet pin).

Following someone now tells them. followUser in the social layer updated the follow indexes and the metrics counter but never created the notification every sibling action creates (like, comment, mention, share and pack join all call createNotification) — so a followed user heard nothing, and testers saw only message notifications. A NEW follow now creates exactly one 'follow' notification for the followed user ('started following you' — the verb phrase the notification UI renders after the actor's name, and the same verb its grouping code uses), carried through the existing presenter (actorId + message) and the socket push inside createNotification. A repeat follow notifies nothing; unfollow + re-follow is a new follow and notifies again. The UI side needed nothing: NotificationCenter already had the follow type, the Follows filter and the follow navigation leg — it was waiting on this row. Pins: new server suite 3/3 (one notification, correct type/actor/content, unread count moves, follower's own inbox empty, repeat silent, re-follow re-notifies) with the shipped emergent-social-layer suite green beside it (48/48 combined) and feed/self-DM suites green; pristine control fails 0/3.

The sidebar 'Search social' and Explore's 'Find people' now search the same people. They read different stores: Find people (GET /users/search) matches the account registry (users table by username) plus social profiles by display name, while the sidebar search (searchSocial) matched people ONLY in the social-profiles map — so anyone with an account but no social profile yet was findable in Explore and invisible in the sidebar, which 'found none' for the same name. searchSocial's people leg now unions the account registry too (active accounts, username match, the same query shaping as /users/search), deduped against the profile hits with the profile's display name winning, and the blocked filter applied to both legs; without a db the profiles-only result stands. Pins: new server suite 2/2 (account-only person found; both-sources person appears once with the profile name; inactive account and blocked person stay out) with the shipped social-feeds and users-search route suites green, and the FE social-feeds/core-loop suites green (7/7); the union test fails on the pristine tree.

The blank megaphone items and the 99+ bell were the autogen pipeline's operator proposals, misread as user notifications. STATE.queues.notifications is a shared array: enqueueNotification feeds it genuine user notifications AND the cognitive worker's dtu_proposal candidates (a DTU payload, no title, addressed to no user, queued for operator review). The user-facing /api/notifications routes listed and counted the whole array, so the panel mapped each proposal to a 'system' item with an empty message (the mapper finds no message/description in a DTU payload) and the badge summed every accumulated, never-read proposal as unread. The routes (list, count, read-all, read-one, delete) now apply one discriminator — isUserNotification (new server/lib/notification-queue.js) — alongside their existing targetUserId scoping: proposals never reach a user's list, count or badge, and the user surface cannot mark or delete them. The proposals stay in the queue untouched for their real readers (the state snapshot's operator view). Pins: new unit suite 2/2 (discriminator + a 60-proposal/3-notification queue selecting exactly the caller's 2, unread 1, proposals intact); control with the discriminator disabled fails 0/2; server.js imports cleanly (boot smoke) and its diff is exactly the import + the five route applications (6 hunks, +9/-5).

Deleting a Quick Capture's DTU now removes the capture's lens artifact too. A capture is one record in two stores: the lens artifact (what the lens Export JSON lists) and its create-exhaust DTU (the vault record). dtu.delete previously removed only the DTU, leaving the artifact exporting forever with no delete path anywhere. The delete macro now cascades from the CREATE exhaust only (machine.kind lens_exhaust + action create + artifactId): the artifact leaves the store and the domain index, with a delete exhaust emitted for its lifecycle, exactly as lens.delete does. Narrow by construction: update/run/export exhaust deletes never cascade; a published or public artifact keeps its life beyond the pointer (no cascade); an artifact already deleted lens-side is a no-op; the cascade requires the artifact owner to match the DTU owner (they are minted together). Pins: new server suite 4/4 on a real booted server (cascade removes artifact from store/list/get · update-exhaust delete spares it · published spares it · plain DTU delete touches nothing); pristine control 3 pass / 1 fail (only the cascade leg); world-observatory full-build 3/3 and the artifact/list suites 41/41 beside it. Premise verified first-hand by an in-process probe at branch state before the fix (artifact survived dtu.delete in store, list and export).

The Photos import decoded every file and re-encoded it as PNG through a canvas, destroying the original format and its EXIF before the server saw it.
